title: Permutation and randomisation tests
dek: If a null makes some reshuffles of the labels exchangeable, the permutation distribution of a statistic is an exact (or exact-given-the-sample) reference. No χ² required.
story: A permutation test is not a bootstrap. The bootstrap approximates a sampling law of an estimator. A permutation test builds a reference law of a test statistic under a sharp null that says certain labels were exchangeable.

Randomised experiments are the cleanest home: under H₀ of no treatment effect, the assignment vector can be reshuffled as the design would have allowed. The p-value is the fraction of assignments as extreme as the one you ran. Coverage of that p-value is by design, not by a Normal limit.

Observational genomics: permuting phenotype against genotype approximates a no-association null only if the permutation respects structure (batches, relatedness, population). A naive shuffle “proves” association with ancestry because ancestry was not exchangeable.
deep: Fisher’s exact test is a permutation test on a 2×2 table, conditioning on margins. It is exact under that conditional null. It is not the only 2×2 test, and it is conservative if you wanted a different unconditional model.

Multiple testing: Westfall–Young permutes and takes the max statistic, capturing dependence among tests. Bonferroni uses a union bound and ignores that dependence. In GWAS, permutation of a structured sample is expensive and still needs a kinship-aware shuffle or a mixed-model null.

Permutation of residuals in regression can test a coefficient when the null model’s fitted structure is kept. Permuting Y against a column of X while leaving confounders unpermuted is the usual mistake — it breaks the relationship between Y and the confounders.
A huge permutation p = 0.00001 is still a p-value under a null. It is not an effect size and not a posterior. Combine with the scientific contrast (risk difference, OR, MIC shift).

formulas.label: Permutation p-value (with +1)
formulas.note: The +1 avoids claiming p = 0 after finite shuffles.

formulas.label: Exchangeability under H₀
formulas.expression: law(Y | assignment) = law(Y | π(assignment))  under H₀
formulas.note: The design’s allowed π are the only legal shuffles.

visual.caption: Permutation as a design-respecting loop: freeze the outcomes, reshuffle only what the null says was random, recompute T, sit T_obs in that cloud. A bootstrap loop would instead resample the world of T as an estimator.

example.title: Shuffle a treatment, not a kinship
example.setup: 20 household clusters, binary treatment assigned at household level, outcome: incident TB. Statistic T = difference in household rates.

steps.title: Legal shuffle
steps.body: Reassign the 20 treatment labels to households as the randomisation would have. Keep members together. Recompute T*.

steps.title: Illegal shuffle
steps.body: Shuffle person-level labels, breaking households. The null distribution is too tight (or just wrong) because it pretends a randomisation you did not run.

steps.title: GWAS cousin
steps.body: Shuffling case/control labels without regard to principal components of ancestry is the same crime: the labels were not exchangeable under a null that still has structure.

example.takeaway: Permute what the null made random. Structure that remains under H₀ must stay in the shuffle.

whyWrong.When you use a +1 p-value: That is a small-sample convention, not a wrong null.
